subject: science
promptStrong: Give me a challenging KS3 exam-style question on {lo}, then mark my answer.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for KS3 simply, with a worked example and the most common mistake.
learningObjectives: Speed and the equation speed = distance / time
Forces as pushes and pulls from interactions

questions.lo: Speed and the equation speed = distance / time
questions.q: Which equation correctly gives the average speed of a moving object?
questions.explain: Speed is how much distance is covered each second, so speed = distance ÷ time. The units are metres per second (m/s).

questions.lo: Speed and the equation speed = distance / time
questions.q: A cyclist travels 240 m in 20 s. What is her average speed?
questions.explain: speed = distance ÷ time = 240 ÷ 20 = 12 m/s.

questions.lo: Speed and the equation speed = distance / time
questions.q: A train moves at a steady 25 m/s for 8 s. How far does it travel?
questions.explain: Rearrange the equation: distance = speed × time = 25 × 8 = 200 m.

questions.lo: Speed and the equation speed = distance / time
questions.q: Why is the value from speed = distance ÷ time usually called the AVERAGE speed for a journey?
options: Because the object never actually moves
Because most journeys speed up and slow down, so the speed varies along the way
Because it is always measured in km/h
Because speed can never be measured exactly
questions.explain: Real journeys speed up and slow down, so a single moment's speed differs from the whole-trip figure. Distance ÷ time gives the average over the whole journey.

questions.q: On a distance–time graph, what does a horizontal (flat) line show?
options: The object is moving at constant speed
questions.explain: A flat line means the distance is not changing as time passes, so the object is stopped.

questions.q: On a distance–time graph, what does a STEEPER straight line mean compared with a less steep one?
questions.explain: The gradient (steepness) of a distance–time graph is the speed. A steeper line covers more distance in the same time, so the object is moving faster.

questions.q: A distance–time graph shows a straight line that slopes upward at a constant gradient. What is the object doing?
questions.explain: A straight sloping line has a constant gradient, so the speed is constant — the object moves at a steady speed.

questions.q: Two cars drive the SAME way along a road, one at 28 m/s and one at 20 m/s. How fast does the faster car move relative to the slower one?
questions.explain: For objects moving the same direction, subtract the speeds: 28 − 20 = 8 m/s. The faster car slowly pulls ahead.

questions.q: Two trains travel toward each other on parallel tracks, one at 30 m/s and one at 25 m/s. How fast do they approach each other?
questions.explain: Moving in opposite directions, the speeds add: 30 + 25 = 55 m/s. They close the gap very quickly.

questions.lo: Forces as pushes and pulls from interactions
questions.q: Which statement about forces is correct?
options: A force is a push or pull that arises from two objects interacting
A single object stores a force by itself
A force is measured in metres per second
Only moving objects can have forces on them
questions.explain: A force is a push or a pull, and it always comes from an interaction between two objects. Forces are measured in newtons (N).

questions.lo: Forces as pushes and pulls from interactions
questions.q: Which instrument is used to measure the size of a force?
questions.explain: A newtonmeter (a spring balance) measures force in newtons — the bigger the force, the more its spring stretches.

questions.q: Which of these is a NON-CONTACT force?
questions.explain: Gravity acts at a distance without objects touching, so it is a non-contact force. Friction, air resistance and a hand's push all need contact.

questions.q: A magnet pulls a steel paperclip toward it across a small air gap. What type of force is this?
questions.explain: Magnetism acts across a gap without the objects touching, so it is a non-contact force.

questions.q: When the forces on an object are balanced (equal and opposite), what happens to its motion?
options: Its motion does not change — it stays still OR moves at a steady speed
questions.explain: Balanced forces cancel out, so there is no change in motion. That means the object is either stationary or moving at a steady speed in a straight line.

questions.q: A car travels along a flat, straight road at a steady 30 m/s. What can you say about the forces on it?
options: They must be zero because it is moving
They are unbalanced, pushing it forward
They are balanced, so its speed stays the same
There are no forces on a moving car
questions.explain: Steady speed in a straight line means no change in motion, so the forces are balanced — the driving force equals friction and air resistance. Balanced does not mean stopped.

questions.q: A rocket accelerates upward, going faster and faster as it climbs. What does this tell you about the forces on it?
options: The forces are unbalanced, with a resultant force upward
questions.explain: A change in motion (speeding up) means the forces are unbalanced. The upward thrust is greater than the weight, giving a resultant force upward.

questions.q: The turning effect of a force about a pivot is called its...
questions.explain: The turning effect of a force is its moment, found from moment = force × distance from the pivot.

questions.q: Why is it easier to loosen a stiff bolt with a long spanner than a short one, using the same push?
options: A greater distance from the pivot gives a bigger moment
There is more friction with a long spanner
questions.explain: Moment = force × distance from the pivot. A longer spanner increases the distance, so the same push produces a larger turning effect.

questions.q: Which equation gives the pressure a force produces on a surface?
questions.explain: Pressure is how concentrated a force is on each bit of area, so pressure = force ÷ area, measured in N/m².

questions.q: A crate pushes down with a force of 600 N over an area of 3 m². What pressure does it exert on the floor?
questions.explain: pressure = force ÷ area = 600 ÷ 3 = 200 N/m².
